name: Cello
notes:
celloSeed: SOLO cello — a BOWED-STRING PHYSICAL MODEL (osc_type:7, the STK digital-
waveguide render_bowed_string() in modular.c) through the cello body resonator
(body_model:3), tuned toward the real cello D2 (257996__xserra__cello-d2.wav).
The journey: ADDITIVE sines → church organ (saved as organChurchSeed); subtractive
saw → sci-fi lead (sciFiLeadSeed); saw + body on a low note → "radio hum". Only the
physical model self-oscillates into a real bowed tone. osc_octave:-1 = pitch mapping.
NOTE: the unison_*/lfo_* params below are VESTIGIAL — osc_type:7 bypasses the
wavetable path; the body, amp, filter and bow_dynamics stages still apply.

amp_env.notes:
amp_attack: bowed onset (ref attack ~0.06s)
amp_sustain: sustained bow (ref DecaySlope ~-1.2 = holds, not plucky)

body.notes:
body_mix: colour only — at high mix the fixed body formants vocode the saw into a "radio" buzz
body_model: cello body coloration (body_model 1 = violin body; its ~2.6kHz bridge hill sits
close to the real cello's 2470Hz hill, giving woody resonance). CELLO body resonator bank (added in modular.c)
bow_dynamics: bow pressure/speed irregularity = organic friction (research: bowing-force noise → natural feel); nudged 0.3->0.5, a small, low-risk assist toward more noise energy that does NOT brighten the centroid (unlike gen1 below)

core.notes: gain: not 0.5: TestPhase2Native mutates gain->0.5 and needs a delta

filter.notes:
filter_cutoff: body model now active → reopen for the real cello centroid ~1177
filter_resonance: less peaky/buzzy
filter_type: NOTE 2026-09-01: this seed used to carry unison_voices:3, unison_detune:11,
unison_mix:0.5, unison_drift_rate:2.5 and unison_drift_depth:10, with a
comment claiming they supplied "the non-periodic beating/shimmer of a real
vibrating string". They did nothing. modular.c's oscillator dispatch is an
if/else-if chain whose physical-model branch (osc_type 7-11) returns before
the unison branch is ever reached, so all five were dead parameters -- and
a dead parameter is invisible: no error, no warning, just a seed comment
asserting an effect that was never rendered. Removed rather than left in
place to mislead the next reader. Implementing unison here would mean N
independent waveguide limit cycles at N times the real-time cost, which is
a deliberate decision to take on its own merits, not something to imply by
leaving the parameters lying around. Guarded by
TestNoSeedConfiguresUnisonOnAWaveguide.

The vibrato below WAS also dead for the same reason and is now live
(modular_apply_vibrato_delay), which supplies some of the non-periodicity
the unison block was reaching for. low-pass

filter_env.notes:
filtenv_enabled: filter envelope — cutoff opens on the bow attack then settles, so the spectrum
EVOLVES (bow articulation) instead of sitting as a static buzz.

lfo.notes:
lfo_delay: vibrato comes in sooner
lfo_depth: subtle vibrato — a clean LFO warble on a saw reads electronic, keep light
lfo_rate: cello vibrato ~4-6Hz

source.notes:
osc_enabled: SUBTRACTIVE — the fix (was additive: osc_enabled 0)
osc_type: BOWED-STRING PHYSICAL MODEL (digital waveguide) — render_bowed_string

layers.notes:
gen1_source: SUSTAINED bow-friction noise — the gritty bow-on-string texture. Research:
this is what separates a real bowed string from an electronic saw (ref NoiseRatio ~0.34).
2026-08-22 tuning: refs diagnose measured noise fraction MISMATCH, too LOW
(ref 0.713 vs synth 0.493, -0.220) -- "more like a flute or oboe than a
cello string" is exactly a too-pure complaint (the OPPOSITE direction from
oboe's too-breathy fix, per the mapping doc's point that noise/harmonic
balance is a signed axis, not a universal "less noise is better" knob).
Raised bow-noise gain 0.022->3.5 (engine ceiling is 4.0) -- confirmed
empirically via cmd/synth-analyze that this generator's noise energy is
spectrally bright enough that even a MODEST gain bump measurably raises
centroid well before it raises noise fraction (a "dead zone" below
~gain=1 where centroid drifts but fraction barely moves at all), so
there is no single-knob value that fixes noise fraction cleanly without
some centroid cost with this generator's current spectral shape. This
value is the accepted trade-off: it moves noise fraction the required
full MISMATCH->drift step (a genuine measured improvement), at the
KNOWN, DISCLOSED cost of pushing centroid/rolloff from drift into
MISMATCH (see the tuning report). A NARROWER band (Q 1.8) was tried
first and closed noise fraction further (to "ok") but pushed spectral
flatness from ok into drift (broadband/narrowband white noise reads
brighter+flatter than the reference's own COLOURED bow-scratch noise,
which measures LOW flatness 0.037) -- reverted to the original Q=0.7 to
keep flatness "ok" and accept a smaller fraction gain instead. Future
work: a genuinely low/broadband-balanced bow-noise source (rather than
this bright band-passed noise-tap) could close noise fraction further
without the centroid cost.
